what_happened: Job 20261031-095235-zq9x was the retry of b5hm, the job that adds a hold when disk is low. It failed on low disk before the verifier ran. Its test check had also failed after 184 seconds, possibly because the disk was full. The person running Athena deleted zq9x's build folders by hand. This gave the next job and zq9x's retry room to run. The failure was an environment stop. No acceptance criterion was found unmet. The failed test check was not judged against a baseline.
cause: Athena owns no disk lifecycle. Build folders from producers, verify-side builds and checks are regenerable but never reclaimed or counted against a disk budget. The 10 GB guard only reports failure and frees nothing. The fix, b5hm, is itself a job that needs disk to run, so it keeps hitting the gap it is meant to close. It was left queued without urgency through four earlier hand cleanups. A disk-full test failure also looks like a real test failure, because nothing checks free space before the checks run, so a failed check may be an environment symptom.
prevention: Make Athena own disk lifecycle in code. (1) After each stage ends, delete that stage's regenerable build folders: the producer build before checks, and the verify-side build after the baseline checks. (2) Before the checks, if free disk is below the guard, reclaim reclaimable space automatically, then re-measure. If it is still low, hold the job as environment-paused rather than failed. A hold does not count as spend. (3) Mark any check failure that happens while free disk is below the guard as environment-suspect, and rerun it after reclaiming space instead of recording a test failure. (4) Run the disk fix with priority and with enough free space, with the the person running Athena clearing disk once before it starts.
proposed_request: Make Athena manage disk itself so a job never ends failed because of low disk. Outcomes: (1) Once a job's producer or baseline-check stage ends, Athena deletes that stage's regenerable build folders before the next stage. (2) Before the checks stage, if free disk is under the 10 GB guard, Athena first reclaims regenerable space (finished build folders, caches, stale scratch worktrees) and measures again. If space is still low, the job is held in a resumable environment-paused state with the shortfall shown. It does not end failed, and the hold does not count as line spend in the scope guard. (3) A check that fails while free disk is under the guard is recorded as environment-suspect and rerun once after space is reclaimed, and the record keeps both results. (4) Show the free-disk figure and what was reclaimed in the job's records. Acceptance: tests with a fake low-disk measure show that (a) reclaim runs and the job proceeds when it frees enough, (b) the job is held and can be resumed when it does not, (c) a check failure under low disk is rerun and flagged, and (d) no regenerable folder is deleted while its stage is still running. This supersedes the queued b5hm and hs8s requests. Run it at urgent priority.
